question_text: Which part of the plant is best suited for making virus-free plants and why?

insider_note: Meristem is the answer and the reason is its rapid division. Name the part in two or three lines, then give the reason.

Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production (Botany-II) · 2 marks

steps.label: The part
steps.margin_note: Both meristems named and the technique. Three lines.
lines: The APICAL and AXILLARY MERISTEMS are best
A SHOOT TIP culture is the standard method.
steps.why: Even in a plant that is systemically infected, the meristem itself is usually free of virus, which is why it is the part to culture.
common_mistakes: Naming the leaf or the root. It is the MERISTEM — the apical or axillary one.
Naming the technique but not the part. The question asks which PART — the apical or axillary meristem.
steps.memory_tip: Take the very tip, where the virus has not reached.

steps.label: The reason
steps.margin_note: Both reasons: the speed of division and the missing vascular connection.

lines.text: Meristem cells divide faster than the virus

lines: Meristematic regions show ACTIVE, RAPID CELL
The cells divide faster than the virus can move
into them, and meristems have no vascular
connection for the virus to travel along.
So the meristem cells are NOT INFECTED, and a
plant raised from them is virus free.
steps.why: A virus spreads mainly through the vascular tissue, and a meristem has none yet — so it stays ahead of the infection.
common_mistakes: Saying the meristem kills the virus. It simply outgrows it and is never infected.
Giving the part with no reason. The question says 'and why'.
steps.memory_tip: The tip grows away from the infection faster than it can follow.
